clinician.trajectory_summary: 51-year-old male presented with acute left-sided flank pain, nausea, and vomiting following minor twisting trauma. CT angiography demonstrated left renal non-enhancement secondary to suspected acute left renal artery dissection. After multidisciplinary consultation, heparin anticoagulation was initiated for renal salvage. The patient was emergently transferred to a higher level of care where angiography confirmed complete lack of flow to the left kidney. Despite initial anticoagulation, the kidney progressed to necrosis requiring nephrectomy.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Acute left-sided flank pain with nausea and vomiting following minor twisting trauma without direct impact
CT angiography revealed left renal non-enhancement secondary to suspected acute traumatic left renal artery dissection
Multidisciplinary consultation (trauma and vascular surgery) recommended heparin anticoagulation for renal salvage
Transfer to higher level of care with angiography demonstrating complete lack of flow to the left kidney confirming vascular compromise
Progression to renal necrosis necessitating nephrectomy as definitive management

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.alternative: Other intra-abdominal traumatic injuries (splenic laceration, liver injury, bowel injury)
ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: CT angiography focused on renal vascular injury without mention of other solid organ damage; clinical course isolated to renal ischemia
Imaging demonstrated vascular flow compromise rather than parenchymal contusion

remaining_uncertainties: Pathology confirmation of renal infarction/necrosis from nephrectomy specimen
Contralateral renal function and long-term renal outcome
Blood pressure management and control status
